reviewedBy: implementation worker for the parallel18 BatchScale rebinding (not independent acceptance)
rationale: I reviewed the complete rebound inventory: the same plan id, original binding, current cells and 12 part ids and kinds, now bound to the BatchScale scene mount (scene:BatchScale, fingerprints from the checker scene registry) instead of the retired TrainingTimeChart mount, with the disclosure moved to the article sentence that introduces the scene as an illustrative calculation. The four external parts and their retained Rudin and Isaac Lab passages are unchanged. The authored, derived and six observed parts are rewritten for the scene, and every retired chart facet is written into a part text: the environment slider and CPU toggle, the FPS, per-iteration and bucket-share readouts, the 49-point sample grid and the Rudin chart markers. All 13 proofs come from one numeric run and one browser run made against the final checker, and the earlier plan and proofs survive unchanged in previous-parallel-plan-and-proofs.json. This is an integrator review, not independent acceptance.

inventory.text: The flat marker labels a reported under-four-minute result, not an equality or a measured x=4096 configuration.
The separate documented simulation/deployment run binds 4096 robots, 24 steps, 98304 transitions/batch, 1500 updates, under twenty minutes and i9-11900k/RTX A6000 hardware.
The original note names Isaac Lab FPS anchors; preserve >900k DextrAH and >1.6M Franka environment-learning FPS at eight RTX PRO 6000 GPUs/16384 envs, distinct from toy throughput.
The CPU toggle is motivated by the specific RTX5090/AMD9800X3D versus two-RTX-PRO-6000/EPYC comparison, not a measured universal toy curve.

The target 2.2e8 transitions, 24 rollout steps as a chosen model input, cost seconds [0.02,4e-6,0.04,0.03,2.2e-5], the fixed-budget assumption, the BatchScale beat-end robot counts (one-batch 64, scale 4,096, cpu 4,096, recap 16,384) and its two curves (solid without and dashed with the assumed per-robot CPU cost) are authored. Retired with the TrainingTimeChart and written in here: the 49-point sample grid (the scene draws exact 32-segment solid and dashed paths) and the flat-marker x (the scene draws no Rudin marker; its near-four-minute 4,096 time is a chosen calibration).

Iterations=target/(robots*24); wall time=iterations*(sim+learn+CPU) with sim 0.02+4e-6*robots, learn 0.04 and CPU 0.03 s, the dashed curve adding 2.2e-5 s per robot to CPU; the time reads in hours or minutes to one decimal, otherwise whole seconds, in the readout sentence and the method text. A fixed formula, not an empirical learning curve. Retired with the TrainingTimeChart: throughput (FPS), per-iteration time, bucket shares and the crossover are no longer rendered, so no observation asserts them; the per-iteration breakdown is still recomputed.

Stepped back three beats from the 16,384-robot recap, the mounted BatchScale scene shows beat one-batch: "64 robots at once: 3.6 hours of training", the method text "64 robots, 3.6 hours", the marker at the 64-robot end of the solid curve, one robot dot and the dashed curve hidden. Retired with the TrainingTimeChart and written in here: the environment slider with its drag and keyboard bounds (beat stepping replaces it) and the aria-pressed CPU toggle (the dashed curve appears at the cpu and recap beats instead). All sibling robot-count and curve states remain required.
